anomalies.observed: R1 is a 10 MΩ resistor from VCC to the gate of the P-MOSFET Q1. Q1 is used as a high-side fan-power switch whose gate is pulled low by NPN Q2 from the PWM signal.
anomalies.expected: A gate pull-up resistor for a PWM-driven PMOS high-side switch should be much lower, typically in the 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ range, so the gate can turn off quickly enough at fan PWM frequency. The value appears three orders of magnitude higher than the other pull-ups on the board.

VCC : C1.1(passive) J5.2(Pin_2,passive) JP1.2(B,passive) Q1.2(S,passive) R1.1(passive) R6.1(passive) U1.3(VI,power_in)

anomalies.impact: The PMOS gate turn-off will be very slow. If the board is intended to switch fan power with the PWM signal, the fan supply may remain partially or fully on, degrading or defeating PWM control and possibly causing unintended fan operation.

parsed.summary: The netlist and SPICE deck are otherwise consistent, but R1 is an unusually high 10 MΩ PMOS gate pull-up in a PWM-driven high-side switch; standard practice would use a much lower value, making this the most likely anomaly.
